meta.confidence_notes: Field structure now locked (nomination day 18 Jul). Johor precedent is fresh and directional but not identical (NS has different ethnic mix and long-standing PH governance). No public NS-specific polls yet; ground reports mixed. Bersatu solo run is a genuine unknown.

executive.headline: A BN+PN government is now the base-case outcome — but the Chinese-majority seat firewall keeps PH in the low-to-mid teens.
executive.subhead: PH governs since 2018 and holds strong Chinese-majority seats around Seremban and Port Dickson. But the Malay-belt swing to BN following the 11 July Johor landslide, combined with Bersatu splintering the opposition Malay vote in only 24 seats, gives the BN-PN informal pact a clear structural advantage.
current_call: **Most likely winner: BN + PN (via informal pact).** BN contests 25 seats, PN 11, no overlap. Combined baseline mean ~20 seats — just past the 19-seat majority threshold. Simulations put ≥19 in the 80-85% range.

**PH holds a floor of ~13-16 seats** anchored by DAP-held Chinese-majority urban Seremban and Port Dickson seats (Bahau, Lobak, Bukit Kepayang, Mambau, Rahang, Chuah, Lukut) plus PKR/Amanah incumbents in Malay-mixed urban wards.

**Bersatu is the wildcard.** Contesting 24 seats solo — no two-way with BN, 16 clashes with BN, 8 with PN. It caps its own seat ceiling but siphons enough Malay-nationalist vote to help PH in narrow Malay-mixed toss-ups (Klawang, Ampangan, Kota, Sikamat).
**The royal dispute has not become a decisive campaign wedge** as of nomination day, though it remains a low-probability, high-impact swing factor.
executive.surprise_scenario: **PH holds government via hung-assembly plurality.** If Bersatu bleeds enough Malay vote from BN in 6-8 rural three-way seats (Sungai Lui, Palong, Juasseh, Seri Menanti, Kota, Gemencheh), and Chinese turnout holds above 70%, PH could reach 17-18 seats — just short of majority — while BN+PN falls to 16-18. A hung assembly then triggers palace intervention over MB appointment. Probability: ~7-10%.

candidates.name: Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan (Tok Mat)
candidates.note: UMNO deputy president, Foreign Minister. Running for a 6th term. Effectively BN's MB-in-waiting though not officially named. Widely popular; incumbency + star + 33% 2023 majority make Rantau close-to-safe.

candidates.name: Anthony Loke
candidates.note: DAP SG, Transport Minister. Defending Chennah since 2013. Straight fight vs MCA. Symbolic seat for DAP prestige — losing would trigger internal reckoning.

candidates.name: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun
candidates.note: Caretaker MB. Left his stronghold Sikamat (won it since 2008) to contest BN-held Linggi (2023 winner Faizal Ramli, 1,461 majority). Bold, potentially reckless: a loss ends his political career.

candidates.name: Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias
candidates.note: Jelebu MP + Negeri Sembilan UMNO chief. Defending Pertang. Coordinates BN state machinery.

candidates.name: Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail
candidates.note: Bersatu high-profile candidate in the seat vacated by Aminuddin. Test case for whether Bersatu can hold Malay-mixed urban seats without PAS.

candidates.name: Nicole Tan
candidates.note: Incumbent since 2018. Straight fight vs PN newcomer. Chinese-super-safe (78% majority in 2023). Bellwether for DAP's Chinese firewall.

candidates.name: Datuk Bakri Sawir
candidates.note: Incumbent Amanah in a Malay-rural three-way vs PN + Bersatu. 2023 margin 6.3% — a canary for the Bersatu-spoiler effect on PH.

risks.title: Royal dispute reignition
risks.note: If the Undang faction escalates via court filing or public statement before 1 Aug, PH loses moral-authority framing and BN gains 1-2 rural Malay seats.

risks.title: Federal cabinet reshuffle / scandal
risks.note: Anwar under pressure post-Johor. A defection or minister resignation would depress PH turnout.

risks.title: Turnout below 65%
risks.note: Johor turnout was 66%. Chinese-voter turnout is the single biggest driver of PH downside — every 5% drop costs PH ~2 Chinese-majority seats.

risks.title: Major viral misinformation event
risks.note: Deepfake or AI-generated race/religion content in final 72h. Historically favours whoever is trailing (currently PH).

risks.title: Bersatu-PAS reconciliation (last-minute PN unity)
risks.note: If Muhyiddin/Hadi announce a joint appeal by 28 Jul, Bersatu could stand-down some candidates. Currently no signal.

risks.title: Kuala Kubu Baharu-style anti-DAP racial campaign
risks.note: Watch Malay-language TikTok for coordinated content targeting Loke, Nicole Tan, Chew Seh Yong.

risks.title: Economic shock (RM/USD, oil price)
risks.note: Ringgit under 4.70/USD watch. Fuel-subsidy timing could re-enter the cycle.

changelog.summary: Baseline forecast v1.0 initialised. BN+PN probability 95%. Field structure locked at nomination day (103 candidates, PH 36, BN 25, PN 11, Bersatu 24, others 7). 12 days to polling.
Nomination day concludes. 21 three-way fights confirmed. BN and PN pact holds — no seat overlap. Bersatu confirmed as opposition splitter in 24 seats.
BN announces 25 candidates, leaves 11 seats for PN. Mohamad Hasan defends Rantau.
PH announces 36 candidates. Aminuddin moves from Sikamat to Linggi. Loke defends Chennah.
Johor state election result: BN 48, PH 8, PN 0. Landslide re-anchors NS model priors toward BN swing.
EC fixes NS polling day 1 Aug; nomination 18 Jul; early vote 28 Jul.
NS state assembly dissolved. Royal dispute escalates in parallel.
